claims: Asteroid 2026 FM3 is passing within 147,836 miles of Earth on March 24-25, 2026.
147,836 miles is roughly 62% of the distance to the Moon.
NASA confirms asteroid 2026 FM3 poses no threat.
Asteroid 2026 FM3 is approximately 13–26 feet (4-8 meters) in size.
Asteroid 2026 FM3 has closest approach at 10:07 p.m. EDT on March 24, 2026.
Asteroid 2026 FM3 closest approach distance is 147,836 miles.
Asteroid 2026 FM3 is traveling at roughly 11,461 miles per hour.
Asteroid 2026 FM3 has zero risk of impact.
Space.com notes asteroid 2026 FM3 is too small to be considered a hazardous asteroid.
According to the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), asteroid 2026 CS (~64 ft) is scheduled to pass by on February 9, 2026, 2.38 million miles away.
According to the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), asteroid 2026 BY1 (~98 ft) is scheduled to pass by on February 9, 2026, 3.87 million miles away.
According to the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), asteroid 2026 BU2 (~34 ft) is scheduled to pass by on February 9, 2026, 4.19 million miles away.
NASA continues to track Potentially Hazardous Asteroids (PHAs).
Potentially Hazardous Asteroids (PHAs) are those larger than 460 feet.
According to Newsweek, none of the Potentially Hazardous Asteroids (PHAs) are projected to hit Earth in the near future.
